kaps_punt: 'n Kaart van Suid-Afrika — See en land op 'n kaart, hoe dit aangedui word; Name van oseane langs die kuslyn van Suid-Afrika; Provinsies, name en ligging op 'n kaart van Suid-Afrika; Hoofstede en dorpe van provinsies; Benaderde ligging van eie nedersetting op 'n kaart van Suid-Afrika

items.bewering: Ons land lê aan die suidkant van die kontinent Afrika.
items.blok: Die see en die land op die kaart
items.bron: GCIS, South Africa Yearbook 2023/24, 'Land and its people', p. 2: the coastline runs 'from the desert border with Namibia on the Atlantic coast southwards around the tip of Africa' (https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/yearbook/2025/yearbook2023-24-1%20Land%20and%20its%20people%202023-24.pdf).

items.bewering: Op so 'n kaart word die see en die land in verskillende kleure gewys. Die see is gewoonlik blou, en die kus is waar die kleur na blou verander. Blou beteken gewoonlik water, en die sleutel sê dikwels wat elke kleur beteken.
items.blok: Die see en die land op die kaart
items.bron: CSUSB 'Mapping basics' (https://www.csusb.edu/sites/default/files/mappingbasics.pdf), from the colour-convention search: blue is used for water features, oceans included. National Geographic Education, 'Map' (https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/map/): a legend is 'a list of the symbols, lines and colors that appear on a map and what they mean', and colours 'can differ drastically from map to map'. That variation is why the lesson's 'gewoonlik' and 'dikwels' are correct. The wording 'the coast is where the colour changes to blue' is about the sea here, so it holds in context. A blue dam or lake on a map also meets the land where the colour changes, but the sentence before this one sets the subject as the sea.

items.bewering: Twee oseane lê langs Suid-Afrika se kus, en elkeen het sy eie naam. Aan die weskus van ons land lê die Atlantiese Oseaan. Die Indiese Oseaan lê aan die ooskus, aan die ander kant van die land.
items.blok: Die kus en die twee oseane
items.bron: GCIS, South Africa Yearbook 2023/24, p. 2: the coast runs from the Namibian border 'on the Atlantic coast' around the tip of Africa 'to the border of subtropical Mozambique on the Indian Ocean'. p. 7 (Western Cape): 'The cold Atlantic Ocean along the West Coast ... while the warmer Indian Ocean skirts the province's southern beaches.' The Northern Cape 'borders the Atlantic Ocean in the west' (p. 6). Note for the person reading: the Indian Ocean also lies along the south coast, east of Cape Agulhas, where the IHO places the boundary. The lesson does not say otherwise; it simply does not assign the south coast. This is incomplete but not false.

items.bewering: Binne ons land se grense lê nege provinsies. Elkeen van hulle het sy eie naam, sy eie grense en sy eie regering.
items.blok: Nege provinsies binne een land
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces' (https://www.gov.za/about-sa/south-africas-provinces): nine provinces, and 'Each province has its own Legislature, Premier and Executive Council.' The Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996, Chapter 6, ss. 104-133 (Wikisource text, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_Republic_of_South_Africa,_1996/Chapter_6), sets up a provincial legislature and executive for each province.

items.bewering: Die grense tussen die provinsies is as lyne op die kaart geteken. Elke provinsie kry gewoonlik ook sy eie kleur op die kaart. Die provinsie se naam staan gewoonlik binne-in sy eie grense gedruk.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n provinsie op die kaart kry
items.bron: Political-map conventions. Wikipedia, 'Four color theorem' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_color_theorem): map regions are coloured so that 'no two adjacent regions have the same color'. National Geographic Education, 'Map': names and borders are labelled, and symbols and colours vary by map. 'Gewoonlik' is right, because colours may repeat between provinces that do not touch. The general political-map pages found were low quality and are not relied on.

items.bewering: Sommige name staan buite die grense, met 'n lyn wat na hul provinsie wys.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n provinsie op die kaart kry
items.bron: Esri, Charlie Frye (Chief Cartographer), ArcGIS blog (https://esri.com/arcgis-blog/?p=121721): labels are offset from small polygons, with 'leader lines to positively associate the label with its feature'. Geography Realm, leader lines in QGIS (https://www.geographyrealm.com/how-to-add-leader-lines-to-labels-in-qgis-3-10/): this is used 'when you are trying to label a small area'. On a map of the whole country this applies to Gauteng, the smallest province (18 178 km², GCIS Yearbook p. 5).

items.bewering: Kaart: die Atlantiese Oseaan langs die weskus en die Indiese Oseaan langs die ooskus, by die naam, sonder 'n grens of ontmoetingspunt tussen die twee oseane
items.blok: kaart (vir: Hoe jy 'n provinsie op die kaart kry)
items.bron: Placement of the two oceans as for the item above (GCIS Yearbook 2023/24, pp. 2, 6, 7). Where the oceans meet is contested. The IHO puts the boundary on the meridian of Cape Agulhas, while popular usage often says Cape Point (search results summarising the IHO definition and the Cape Point view, e.g. https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Diving_in_South_Africa). Leaving the meeting point off the map makes no claim, so the instruction is sound.

items.bewering: Kaart: die nege provinsies, elkeen met sy grense en sy naam; die nege provinsiale hoofstede by die naam ... Johannesburg, Pietermaritzburg, Polokwane, Mbombela, Kimberley, Mahikeng, Bhisho, Bloemfontein en Kaapstad
items.blok: kaart (vir: Hoe jy 'n provinsie op die kaart kry)
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces', and GCIS Yearbook 2023/24, pp. 3-7 (capital boxes). All nine capitals match, and every spelling matches the current official form (Mahikeng, not Mafikeng; Bhisho, not Bisho; Mbombela, not Nelspruit).

items.bewering: Kaart: Die kaart merk geen nasionale hoofstad nie, en Pretoria word nie as 'n hoofstad gemerk nie.
items.blok: kaart (vir: Hoe jy 'n provinsie op die kaart kry)
items.bron: This is a design instruction, not a claim about Pretoria. gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces': Pretoria is the administrative capital, Cape Town the legislative and Bloemfontein the judicial. The instruction leaves out all three national roles alike, and does not say Pretoria is not a capital. It also does not stop Cape Town and Bloemfontein appearing as provincial capitals, which is correct. Nothing false is taught.

items.bewering: Kaart: 'n Buurland binne of langs Suid-Afrika se buitelyn word as 'n ander land gewys en nooit as 'n provinsie nie.
items.blok: kaart (vir: Hoe jy 'n provinsie op die kaart kry)
items.bron: GCIS Yearbook 2023/24, p. 2: 'The country shares common boundaries with Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Eswatini, while the Mountain Kingdom of Lesotho is landlocked by South African territory in the south-east.' Lesotho lies inside the outline; the others lie along it. Both cases are correctly treated as separate countries.

items.bewering: Elke provinsie se regering werk hoofsaaklik vanuit een dorp of stad, en daardie plek is sy hoofstad.
items.blok: Wat 'n hoofstad is
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces' (each province has its own legislature, premier and executive council, and one named capital). Merriam-Webster, 'capital' (https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/capital): 'a city serving as a seat of government'. 'Hoofsaaklik' correctly allows for provincial departments that also have offices elsewhere.

items.bewering: Gauteng — Johannesburg; KwaZulu-Natal — Pietermaritzburg; Limpopo — Polokwane; Mpumalanga — Mbombela; Noord-Kaap — Kimberley; Noordwes — Mahikeng; Oos-Kaap — Bhisho; Vrystaat — Bloemfontein; Wes-Kaap — Kaapstad
items.blok: Die nege provinsies en hul hoofstede
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces' (https://www.gov.za/about-sa/south-africas-provinces), which lists exactly these nine pairs. Each pair was also checked against the capital box for its province in the GCIS Yearbook 2023/24, pp. 3-7. The Afrikaans province names (Noord-Kaap, Noordwes, Oos-Kaap, Vrystaat, Wes-Kaap) are the standard forms.

items.bewering: Durban lê byvoorbeeld in KwaZulu-Natal, Upington in die Noord-Kaap en Welkom in die Vrystaat.
items.blok: Ander dorpe en stede
items.bron: GCIS Yearbook 2023/24: Durban, under KwaZulu-Natal (p. 5, 'the port of Durban'); Upington, under Northern Cape (p. 6, 'two major airports at Kimberley and Upington'); Welkom, under Free State (p. 3, 'Important towns include Welkom'). gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces', also lists Welkom under the Free State.

items.bewering: Behalwe sy hoofstad het elke provinsie ook ander dorpe en stede.
items.blok: Ander dorpe en stede
items.bron: GCIS Yearbook 2023/24, pp. 3-7: each provincial section names further towns besides its capital, e.g. Welkom and Kroonstad (Free State), eMalahleni and Standerton (Mpumalanga), Rustenburg and Klerksdorp (North West).

items.bewering: 'n Kaart van die hele land het nie plek vir elke plaas en dorpie nie. Soek dan binne daardie grense die naaste dorp of stad wat wel daar staan. So weet jy naastenby waar jou eie plek lê.
items.blok: Soek nou jou eie plek
items.bron: 'Naaste' is grammatically a superlative, but here it is a reading instruction and makes no factual claim of a record. The claim that a national map leaves out small places rests on cartographic generalisation: University of Twente ITC glossary, 'Cartographic generalization' (https://ltb.itc.utwente.nl/659/concept/174062), where selection depends on scale and small-scale maps show only the larger settlements. Karsznia and Sielicka, ISPRS Int. J. Geo-Inf. 2020, 9, 230 (settlement selection for small-scale maps). 'Naastenby' correctly limits what the method gives.

items.bewering: 'n Blanko kaart van Suid-Afrika wys gewoonlik net die kus en die grense, sonder name. Kyk op die voltooide kaart watter lyne om elke plek lê. Soek dieselfde lyne op jou eie kaart en skryf die naam daarbinne of kleur die plek in.
items.blok: Van 'n voltooide kaart na jou eie kaart
items.bron: This describes an outline (blank) map: borders and coast drawn, labels left out. It follows from the legend and labelling conventions above (National Geographic Education, 'Map'). 'Gewoonlik' covers blank maps that also show rivers or towns as dots. Nothing in it can mislead.

items.bewering: land: 'n Gebied met sy eie grense wat homself regeer, soos Suid-Afrika.
items.blok: begrip: land
items.bron: Standard simplification of a sovereign state: a defined territory with borders and its own government, independent in its affairs (summaries from the sovereign-state search; Wikipedia, 'Province', https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province, for the contrast that a province is a division within a country). Read alone, 'homself regeer' is what separates a country from a province, which only has 'sy eie regering' as part of a country. The definition is not false. It is close to the province entry, though, and the 'provinsie' entry ('deel van 'n land') carries the distinction. The lesson also uses 'land' in a second sense, land as opposed to sea, in 'Die see en die land' and in the 'kus' entry. That is a language and clarity matter, not a factual error.

items.bewering: grens: Die lyn wat een gebied van 'n ander gebied skei.
items.blok: begrip: grens
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Map', where lines on a map represent borders between areas. Merriam-Webster 'border/boundary' sense: a line that marks the limit of an area. The definition is accurate and covers both national and provincial borders, as the lesson uses it.

items.bewering: kus: Die deel van die land wat langs die see lê.
items.blok: begrip: kus
items.bron: Royal Geographical Society lesson material (https://www.rgs.org/media/fzabqtti/coastslesson1lessonplan.doc) and Kapow Primary glossary ('a piece of land along the sea or ocean'). These are educational glossaries rather than a dictionary, but the sense is uncontested and matches the common dictionary definition of 'coast' as land next to the sea.

items.bewering: provinsie: 'n Deel van 'n land met sy eie grense en regering.
items.blok: begrip: provinsie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Province': an administrative division within a country. For South Africa, gov.za says each province has its own legislature, premier and executive council, so 'sy eie ... regering' is accurate here. Some countries' provinces have little self-government, but the lesson is about South Africa.

items.bewering: hoofstad: 'n Dorp of stad vanwaar 'n land of provinsie regeer word.
items.blok: begrip: hoofstad
items.bron: Merriam-Webster, 'capital': 'a city serving as a seat of government'. The definition is accurate for provinces. For South Africa as a country, government is split across three capitals (gov.za: Pretoria administrative, Cape Town legislative, Bloemfontein judicial). The singular 'n dorp of stad' is a general definition, not a claim that South Africa has only one. The lesson names no national capital anywhere, so no false number is taught.

opsomming: Every checkable claim holds: the nine provinces and capitals (current official spellings Mahikeng, Bhisho, Mbombela), Durban, Upington and Welkom in their provinces, Atlantic west and Indian east, Lesotho and the neighbouring countries in the map block, and all five definitions were confirmed against gov.za and the GCIS South Africa Yearbook 2023/24. The lesson has no superlatives except the instruction 'naaste dorp' and no comparisons whose mapping could mislead. For a person only, not a fault: the Indian Ocean also lies along the south coast, which the lesson leaves unassigned, and 'land' is used both for a country and for land as opposed to sea.
